alex_foley: FYI opened a docs PR to update the model card for oboro-6b and the catalog entry - https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4728
alex_foley: Summary: clarifies supported sequence lengths, adds a small throughput benchmark table, updates SDK snippets to sdk-v4, and notes CPU-quant fallback behavior. Requesting quick sanity check before merge window. :wave:
maria_garner: Quick skim — the seq_limit in the card is listed as 8192 but our bench was done at 4096. Did we increase the verified limit?
alex_foley: Good catch. Bench used 4096 but we had earlier stress test for 8192 in a separate branch. I left 8192 because runtime supports it, but note says "recommended for production ≤4096". Want to avoid confusion. Should we make the doc explicit?
maria_garner: Yeah make it explicit. Maybe write: "technical max: 8192 (untested under sustained load); recommended production ceiling: 4096 for 99th%-tile latency SLOs." Short and clear.
liam_khan: Also drop-in note about KV cache memory growth for long sequences — add a line in compatibility notes: "KV cache memory scales O(seq_len) - enable prefix-caching for repeated conversational contexts."
sophie_docs: @alex_foley can you swap the SDK snippet to use the v4 async streaming example and change param name `max_tokens` -> `max_new_tokens`? We had a bunch of reported mismatches in the migration tracker.
alex_foley: Sure. Current snippet: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="oboro-6b", prompt="summarize: ...", max_tokens=256)
print(resp.text)
```
alex_foley: I'll replace with async streaming example and update param names. New snippet candidate: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async with client.stream_generate(model="oboro-6b", prompt="summarize: ...", max_new_tokens=256) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end="")
```
sophie_docs: That looks good. Add a one-liner about error behavior when quant fallback occurs: "If CPU fallback is used, cold-starts may be slower and throughput may drop ~3-5x; see runtime-fallback section."
ravi_ops: CI job flagged one linter issue (linking to internal bench CSV stored in s3). ci-bot: check failed on docs-link-check for https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-bench/oboro-6b/2026-03-21.csv
maria_garner: For the throughput table please include hardware spec row (gpus, batch sizes, seq len), otherwise numbers are confusing. Small table with three rows is fine.
alex_foley: Will add hardware column and re-run bench link. Also will add the explicit seq_limit wording + KV cache note + updated SDK snippet + quant-fallback sentence.
liam_khan: One extra: add a short compatibility checkbox list at top: supported runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private), quantized variants supported (yes/no), recommended batch/window config. Makes it easier for platform folks.
sophie_docs: After you push edits I'll do a quick pass and then merge. Prefer to avoid big prose changes — just make the clarifications. :+1:
ci-bot: build/test 4728 — docs-link-check: FAILED (1 broken link)
alex_foley: I'll fix the S3 path and push. ETA 30m.
maria_garner: Thanks — if you can ping here when pushed I'll verify the bench numbers match. :eyes:
alex_foley: Pushed. link fix and snippet updated. Also added hardware row and the "technical max / recommended" language. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4728
sophie_docs: LGTM, small nits inline but not blocking. Merging after CI green.
ci-bot: build/test 4728 — docs-link-check: PASSED
alex_foley: Merged. Thanks everyone — added a short follow-up issue to track full 8k sustained-load validation (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/issues/221).
